 The returning James Maddison scored a beauty, with Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies also on target as Spurs won in the league for the first time this season
  Updated  12m ago Daniel Harris Mon 19 Oct 2026 17.08 EDT First published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 13.30 EDT Share Key events 19m ago The league table

 1h ago GOAL! Tottenham Hotspur 1-1 Coventry City (Rudoni 50)

 11m ago 17.08 EDT Righto, Jacob Steinberg’s match report is here: 
 Davies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against Coventry Read more As such, we’re finished here. Thanks for your company and comments; peace out.
 Share 14m ago 17.06 EDT The absolute state of this ailing thing of ours. Why can’t people just be alright?
 Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme Read more Share 16m ago 17.04 EDT “How many teams manage to double both their points and goals scored in a single day in mid-October?” wonders Phil Moseley. 
 Yup, and Spurs have some winnable games coming up too. Chelsea away this weekend will be tricky but then comes Palace home, Leeds away, Ipswich home, Sunderland away, Fulham home. We’ll have a decent idea of the kind of season they’ll have at the end of that run.
 Share 19m ago 17.01 EDT The league table
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: The Guardian Share 20m ago 16.59 EDT FULL TIME: Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 Coventry City
 A terrific night for Spurs, Maddison making a scoring return, Kulusevski also coming back, and a first league win of the season. They didn’t play especially well but they’ll be better for this, while Coventry again showed enough to suggest they’ve a chance of staying up.
 Share 22m ago 16.58 EDT 90+7 min The third goal is, in a way, just reward for trying to score it – last week, Spurs benefited from a side too scared to pursue a clincher, a mistake they’ve not made themselves.
 Share 23m ago 16.57 EDT GOAL! Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 Coventry City (Davies 90+6)
 After 148 days, Tottenham are going to win a league game! Tel does well to take time out of the game and, when his cross is cleared to the edge, an important touch from Solanke allows Davis to swipe a low trivela that arcs just inside the near post. Relief inside the ground!
 View image in fullscreen Ben Davies. Who’d have thought it? Photograph: Ashley Western/COLORSPORT/Shutterstock Share Updated at  17.06 EDT 24m ago 16.55 EDT 90+5 min Tel keeps the ball in the corner, then his cross is cleared to the edge of the box…
 Share Updated at  16.56 EDT 25m ago 16.54 EDT 90+4 min The delivery isn’t bad but Van de Ven heads clear at the front post and Spurs are halfway there.
 Share 26m ago 16.53 EDT 90+3 min Coventry opt not to launch a long throw, instead putting a pass into the box and keeping the attack alive well before Mason-Clark wins a corner.
 Share 27m ago 16.52 EDT 90+2 min Now Spurs attack, Tel looking to draw a curler into the far top corner and making out like he was close, but he wasn’t.
 Share 28m ago 16.52 EDT 90+1 min From a seemingly impossible position close to the by-line and Van Hecke in front of him, Mason-Clark drives over a cross that Awoniyi attacks … but can’t quite reach.
 Share 29m ago 16.50 EDT 90 min We’ll have eight additional minutes – just as there were when Spurs were trailing last weekend.
 Share 30m ago 16.49 EDT 89 min Davies leaves one on Kesler-Hatden and Hamer sends the free-kick into the box, Thomas up, but Spurs clear and Kulusevski leads the counter alone, crossing way beyond the far post to no one.
 Share 31m ago 16.48 EDT 88 min Kulusevski was given a proper welcome and his first touches are cheered around the ground; his heart will be doing happy hardcore beats.
 Share 32m ago 16.47 EDT 87 min Coventry, meanwhile, send on Kesler-Hayden for Rudoni.
 Share 33m ago 16.46 EDT 86 min After Maddison’s goal another affirming moment for Spurs, Marmoush going down with what might be cramp, Kulusevski replacing him. He gets the big welcome he deserves; let’s hope he can stay fit now, because if he can, he’s a proper player. Oh and Tel also comes on, with Kudus going off.
 View image in fullscreen He’s back! Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.52 EDT 35m ago 16.45 EDT 84 min Caoventry are now building the play with four men on the last line and Mason-Clark lays back for Dasilva whose cross isn’t bad, but Rudoni can’t quite crane his neck-muscles enough to head at goal.
 Share 36m ago 16.43 EDT 83 min Spurs keep it well, burning time, but I bet there are some fans who half want them to concede now, so they’ve time to seek a winner. Such is the torment of a low-scoring sport.
 Share 38m ago 16.41 EDT 81 min Davies nashes down the left and Spurs again move the ball right to Kudus. Again, he comes infield but this time he crosses and, when the clearance reaches Fernandes, he curls a sidefooter into Rushworth’s arms.
 Share 39m ago 16.40 EDT 80 min Good work from Tonali, who weaves by a couple of challenges in midfield before the ball makes its way out to Kudus, who dips infield to open the angle for a curler, before sending his effort over the bar.
 Share 40m ago 16.39 EDT 79 min Tonali humps out of play, yet more evidence Spurs are feeling this, and if they can’t rely on him to keep the head, who can they rely on? But they do get the long throw away and set off on the attack.
 Share 42m ago 16.38 EDT 78 min Changes for Coventry, Mason-Clark and Hamer replacing Sakamoto and Thomas-Asante, who’s probably been their best player.
 Share 42m ago 16.37 EDT 77 min Thomas-Asante intercepts a poor pass from Gallagher and seeks Rudoni, who can’t quite take the ball away from Van Hecke. Still, though, Spurs look nervous already, a feeling that’ll only intensify as we get nearer full time.
 View image in fullscreen Frustration for Jack Rudoni. Photograph: Jonny Weeks/The Guardian Share Updated at  16.46 EDT 44m ago 16.35 EDT 74 min I guess whatever colour Coventry’s kit is, it looks like what it’s meant to be. The first time I saw Sunderland’s pink Elvis top, not one part of me believed it not to be leisurewear.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Andy Thomas/Every Second Media/Shutterstock Share 47m ago 16.33 EDT 73 min Van Ewijk robs Kudus deep inside the Spurs half and flights a cross to the back post … just over Rudoni. Coventry are playing with the belief that they can equalise.
 Share 48m ago 16.31 EDT 72 min Play resumes with a Coventry throw, Van Eweijk hurling into the box and Spurs heading clear.
 Share 49m ago 16.30 EDT 70 min Changes for Spurs, Davies for Robertson, Gallagher for Maddison – who enjoys the acclaim of the crowd as he departs – and Fernandes for the cramping Tosin. I guess they’ll go to 4-2-3-1.
 Share Updated at  16.30 EDT 51m ago 16.29 EDT 68 min Coventry are building a bit of pressure, a cross-kick into the box allowing Thomas to leap all over Gray, heading back across and forcing Van de Ven to diving head away. Already, it’s a bit panicked and, with so long left, that is not the way spurs want to be defending.
 Share 53m ago 16.27 EDT 67 min “Completely agree about how horrible Parma Violets taset,” says David Wall. “However they’re very useful when ground up if you want to colour the purple layer of a rainbow cake and haven’t got the right food dye. Fortunately the violet flavour is subtle enough that you can’t actually taste it in the cake.”
 That is good information, thanks – though would one not use Fizzers to get the same effect and a bit more action?
 Share 54m ago 16.26 EDT 65 min Coventry are indeed getting Rudoni into the game, as we said they’d have to; he’s drifting about unchecked and lasers a pass into the box that Awoniyi can’t quite get on the end of. As long as it stays 2-1, Coventry have a decent chance of sneaking a point.
 Share 55m ago 16.24 EDT 64 min A fine long pass from Van Hecke sets Solanke at Thomas, right side of the box, and he chops inside well only to see the shooting lanes closed down, thwacking an effort that’s blocked.
 Share 1h ago 16.23 EDT 64 min Tonali runs away from Rudoni, who slides in for the hell of it and snags an ankle; he’s booked, as he knew he would be.
 Share 1h ago 16.23 EDT 62 min Credit to Spurs, by the way, who didn’t feel sorry for themselves after conceding but went after a second goal – which they ought really to have done straight after their first. They’ve not made that mistake this time, though, pushing hard for a clinching third.
 Share 1h ago 16.21 EDT 61 min A double change for Coventry, Onyeka and Awoniyi for Yirenkyi and Cherif.
 Share 1h ago 16.21 EDT 60 min There was proper contact but VAR deems it accidental, which I think is a bit of a touch for Spurs. I guess it’s one of those you’re vexed if you score it and it’s chalked off, but you’re also vexed if it’s scored against you and it isn’t, so it makes some sort of sense to go with the original call.
 Share 1h ago 16.19 EDT ANOTHER LOVELY GOAL! Tottenham Hotspur 2-1 Coventry City (Marmoush 59)
 Marmoush spins Van Ewijk, introducing elbow to nose in the process, feints the shot then, stepping inside, punches a curler from 20 yards that Rushworth gets hands to but can’t keep out. That’s his first goal for Spurs, but will VAR disallow it?
 View image in fullscreen Omar Marmoush lets fly to restore Spurs’ lead! Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  16.45 EDT 1h ago 16.17 EDT 56 min “Coventry’s is kit the same colour as Farage’s blazer on big paper’s lead story,” notes James Chambers.
 What are we calling this? Innocent guv lilac?
 View image in fullscreen Share Updated at  16.39 EDT 1h ago 16.15 EDT 55 min Again, Tonali seizes on a loose ball, swiping studs across it to evade a challenge before welting another shot over the top.
 Share 1h ago 16.14 EDT 52 min We said Spurs would need a second goal and they’re seeking one, Kudus hitting the line and cutting back a decent cross, half-cleared to Tonali, charging in … and he hammers an effort that flies over the top.
